record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures functional alignment between models with causal interchange interventions and compares it with RSA and CKA. This is a different method from the original sources but bears on whether and under what conditions representations align.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported alignment measurements and comparisons of similarity measures. The paper's matrix-count and compute arguments, and CLMAS comparisons that only assess the proposed method's performance, are not recorded as representation-alignment findings for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: A methods paper with its own results on whether models align. Causal interchange (MAS) between different-seed GRUs, a GRU and a transformer, GRUs trained on different tasks, and fine-tuned DeepSeek-1.5B models bears on V3 and V4. MAS compared with RSA, CKA and stitching bears on V6. Task- and data-dependent alignment bears on V7. No scale, vision-language or feature-level analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that MAS is a bidirectional, more causally restrictive and more compute-efficient alternative to model stitching (linear in the number of models). They add that CLMAS improves alignment when one model is causally inaccessible. They frame the toxicity result as a proof of principle for detecting misalignment, not as a claim about convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces MAS, a causal interchange-intervention method with learned alignment functions, rather than reproducing the original sources' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with similarity method (MAS versus RSA/CKA), layer (embeddings versus hidden states), architecture, task, and the numeric variable and value range used.
record.problems: Many cited result values are available only in figures and are not numerically stated in the text. The numeric-task models are described as simplistic proof-of-principle settings. The study does not test model scaling or capability increases, and does not establish the cause of alignment differences.

untested.parts: No vision-language or paired image-caption analysis.
No unit-level or basis-level matching across seeds; only two seeds per task in small GRUs.
No relative representations and no mapping without paired data. Only small numeric-task models, plus relative IIA for the 1.5B LLM.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No sweep of neighbour-count settings and no out-of-distribution inputs.
No plateau with scale. No test of shared data or objectives against a common model of reality.

missing.what: With Pearson instead of Spearman correlation of the same RDMs, RSA returns to near ceiling. This shows the low embedding RSA depends on a metric setting.
Cumu Val and Rem Ops align both between and within Arithmetic GRUs (different seeds).
Self-comparison reference values (dashed lines) for MAS, RSA and CKA, needed as ceilings for r1-r10.

record.verdict_notes: All values are figure-only; the text gives only qualitative descriptions (high, low, comparable). The toxicity models are fine-tunes of one shared base model, so they speak to fine-tuning data only. LSTMs are described in the methods but no LSTM results appear. The models are small (128-dimensional) proof-of-principle networks.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of alignment increasing with scale or capability.
No vision-language comparison or paired image-caption representation analysis.
Tests causal transfer between different-seed GRUs, not whether the same individual features recur or whether shared subspaces are common across a broader set of architectures and tasks.
Tests causal interchange and stitching-style transfer; does not test relative representations or mapping without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Compares MAS, RSA, and CKA and reports layer and task differences, but does not systematically sweep metric settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete and task-dependent alignment; does not isolate whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, nor test a scale-related plateau.
